sources: dossier=Intentional absences: 'userdata_schema and declared_events. Both in the retired-mechanisms list that must not appear as current anywhere (2026-07-11, 3f71f90a, transcript)'; doc=observability.md What-it-is/Boundaries/Invariants named userdata_schema as the current per-service declaration; code=executor.proto reserved field 4 comment ('userdata concept retired 2026-05-21'), zero non-generated Go/proto hits for userdata_schema, live field is executor_observability.proto expected_attributes_schema carried as ExpectedAttributesSchema through handshake.go/template_validator.go/runner_dispatch.go/validation_pipeline.go
note: Dossier explicitly transcript-rules userdata_schema retired and forbids it appearing as current; doc named it as canonical three times. Rewrote observability.md's What-it-is, Boundaries, and Invariants to name the live executor-side expected_attributes_schema instead.

sources: dossier=Intentional absences + Superseded/historical: userdata_schema retired outright (2026-07-11 retired list; per-peer userdata_schema two-gate validation retired 2026-07-11, superseding the 2026-05-11 log-convergence mechanism); doc=lines 11/19/25 named userdata_schema as the per-service validation surface; code=zero hits for userdata_schema in non-generated Go/proto, expected_attributes_schema is the live field (executor_observability.proto:50, ObservabilityCapabilities.ExpectedAttributesSchema, applied at template_validator.go and runner_dispatch.go/validation_pipeline.go)
note: Same defect as row 78/947 (duplicate finding, same passage). Fixed in the same edit: userdata_schema replaced with expected_attributes_schema throughout observability.md.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors: 'Executor trace observability: ... an operator can stream live structured trace events in flight and fetch the full trace after terminal' (2026-06-08, corpus-bootstrap, artifact-only) vs 'Claim-producer observability: fetch claim detail, stream live claim-state changes, paginate the producer's claim inventory, render producer-declared admin views' (2026-06-08, corpus-bootstrap, artifact-only); doc=line 11 said both protocols expose 'single-trace fetch and trace-stream methods'; code=claim_producer_observability.proto RPCs are GetClaim/StreamClaim/ListClaims/GetAdminView (no trace RPCs), executor_observability.proto has GetTrace/StreamTrace
note: Dossier describes the two protocols with distinct capability lists (trace-only for executor, claim-view/list/admin for claim-producer), corroborated independently by the proto RPC lists. Doc's blanket 'single-trace fetch and trace-stream methods for each' was wrong; rewrote What-it-is to describe each protocol's actual methods.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line describing claim-producer observability capabilities (claim fetch/stream/paginate/admin views) never mentions a schema surface, consistent with the executor-only framing implied by the distinct capability vocabularies in lines 10 and 31; doc=lines 11/19/25 called the schema surface 'per-service'; code=expected_attributes_schema exists only on ObservabilityCapabilities (executor_observability.proto:50); ClaimProducerObservabilityCapabilities (claim_producer_observability.proto) has no schema field
note: The schema validation surface is executor-only, not per-service; this correction rides the same edit as row 78/480/947 since it touches the identical passage being rewritten for the userdata_schema->expected_attributes_schema rename. Doc now says 'executor-side expected_attributes_schema' rather than 'per-service'.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Executor-side observability is a separate optional gRPC service, ExecutorObservability, distinct from the required NodeExecutor' framing two distinct service-kind-scoped protocols, not two protocols per single service; doc=line 11 'Two optional gRPC protocols per service'; code=handshake.go ProbeExecutor/ProbeStore are distinct paths, an executor implements only ExecutorObservability and a claim-producer only ClaimProducerObservability
note: Confirmed misleading phrasing: there are two protocols total, one per service kind, and a service implements at most one. Rewrote to 'Two optional gRPC protocols total, one per service kind ... A given service implements at most one, matching its kind.'
